ai.subject: Pathology
ai.summary: Systemic pathology SAQs test your ability to integrate disease mechanisms, clinical presentation and investigations across organ systems. Focus on reasoning, not memorisation, to answer short answer questions effectively.

sections.p: Systemic pathology SAQs are exam items that require concise, reasoned answers about diseases affecting multiple organ systems, linking pathology to clinical findings.

t.b: What tissue changes confirm the diagnosis? → Shows characteristic cellular pattern, guiding definitive diagnosis.
What clinical features satisfy the case definition? → Presence of hallmark signs/symptoms confirms the disease.

sections.p: Use recognized staging systems (e.g., TNM, WHO grades) to grade disease burden and guide management.

t.b: What extent of organ involvement is present? → Determines stage and treatment urgency.

t.b: Is there anemia or leukocytosis? → Anemia suggests chronic disease; leukocytosis may indicate infection.
Is an infectious cause present? → Positive result confirms viral contribution.
Is organ enlargement or effusion present? → Detects hepatosplenomegaly when CT unavailable.

sections.p: Identify features that signal imminent deterioration or organ failure.

Blood transfusion for severe anemia – restore oxygen delivery

sections.p: Treat the underlying cause first, then provide supportive care and monitor response.
